vulnerability_mechanism: Flawed/bypassable manual escaping helper (quoteIfNotQuoted): re-wraps quote-delimited input without re-escaping when input already starts/ends with a quote
source_type: In-app user-generated content (social-network note/status text, local or remote)
sink_type: SQLiteDatabase.execSQL(sql: String) -- single-argument raw execution, no bind-args parameter used at all
propagation_pattern: Single-hop within one file: value -> escaping-helper call -> string concatenation -> execSQL, but the escaping helper itself (a second file, MyQuery.kt) contains the actual logic flaw
android_component: None (internal search-index maintenance utility, not an IPC entry point)
sanitization_failure_type: Attempted-but-flawed: a real escaping function exists and is called, but has a bypassable edge case
code_structure: String concatenation of literal SQL fragments + one escaped(-attempted) value; single execSQL call
reachability: Internal maintenance/checker routine; reachable without external IPC, triggered by the app's own data-integrity-check pass over locally-held content

vulnerability_mechanism: Query-builder API misuse: SupportSQLiteQueryBuilder.selection(selection, selectionArgs) builds a bindable query, but only the resulting .sql text is extracted and forwarded -- the intended bind-args mechanism is silently discarded before reaching the sink
source_type: External IPC caller: ContentProvider.query() selection/selectionArgs parameters, supplied by any app invoking ContentResolver.query() on this exported URI
sink_type: Custom rawQuery(query: String) wrapper -> transactor.usePrepared(query) -- a raw prepared-statement execution of a bare string with no separate bind-args parameter in the call signature
propagation_pattern: Two-file hop: ContentProvider.query() (entry point) -> ContentProviderDaoBlocking.rawQuery() (sink), builder object discarded in between
android_component: ContentProvider (android:exported="true", gated only by a custom app-defined permission)
database_api: androidx.sqlite.db.SupportSQLiteQueryBuilder + a custom rawQuery(String) wrapper around Room's usePrepared()
sanitization_failure_type: Absent entirely: no whitelisting, escaping, or structural validation of the caller-supplied selection text at any point
code_structure: Builder-pattern call chain where the safe half of the API (bind-arg propagation) is dropped by extracting only .sql
reachability: Externally reachable via inter-process communication (any app holding the custom READ_TASKS permission) -- the only sample in this corpus reachable from OUTSIDE the vulnerable app's own process

vulnerability_mechanism: Structured-API misuse: SQLiteDatabase.query()'s selection parameter (designed to be used with '?' placeholders and a separate selectionArgs array) is instead built by direct string concatenation of untrusted data, with selectionArgs left null
source_type: External FILE input: an XML backup/restore file chosen and imported by the user, parsed via SAX with zero validation of attribute content
sink_type: SQLiteDatabase.query(distinct, table, columns, selection, selectionArgs=null, ...) -- the structured query() method, not execSQL or rawQuery
propagation_pattern: Five-file, multi-hop: XML SAX parser (RestoreHandler) -> plain data object (RestoreDataSet/CategoryEntry, no sanitizing accessors) -> restore loop (Restore.java) -> DB helper (DBHelper.addCategory) -- the longest, most indirect propagation chain of the three vulnerable samples
android_component: None (a local file-import/restore feature; not a ContentProvider, not network-facing)
database_api: SQLiteDatabase.query(boolean, String, String[], String selection, String[] selectionArgs, ...)
sanitization_failure_type: Absent entirely: no escaping, whitelisting, or length/character validation anywhere across all 5 hops
code_structure: Concatenation of a single-quote-wrapped literal fragment around an unsanitized field value, passed as the 'selection' argument of an otherwise-safe structured API
reachability: Local/social-engineering vector: requires the user to actively choose to import a maliciously-crafted backup file (not remotely triggerable, not reachable via another installed app)
